newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Persson-Leaders may have to rule on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Persson-Leaders may have to rule on stability pact.

text.p: Sweden's prime minister Goran Persson said on Thursday the EU would soon agree a stability pact to protect its future single currency, but suggested the issue might have to be resolved by heads of government.

Persson told reporters, "I believe that the heads of government will solve (the issue of) the stability pact." Asked if he meant that a deal would be struck on Thursday night at a special session of EU finance ministers, he replied, "during the weekend."
The EU heads of government start a two-day summit on Friday.
Persson said of the discussions about the stability pact, "My feeling is that it will be fairly dramatic."

Sweden's finance minister, Erik Asbrink, told reporters there were still some outstanding issues to be resolved over the stability pact, aimed at curbing fiscal deficits after monetary union is launched in 1999.
"I still believe that the main alternative is that we'll reach agreement at this meeting (of finance ministers)," Asbrink said.
